Riya S.: Quick thread to pick an upgrade lane for private deploys. Field keeps asking for <1h rollback and predictable egress IPs. Need a decision on blue-green vs rolling by Wed so sales can set expectations.
Tom H.: Summary of tradeoffs: blue-green = easier rollback and IP stability (swap floating IPs), but needs double capacity for a short window. rolling = lower peak infra but trickier rollback and IP churn.
Nora (EngOps): From ops POV: blue-green lets us validate new control-plane config in an isolated environment. Rolling can be done safely for stateless components but DB schema changes still block rollback. For GA, suggest limiting blue-green to infra/config-only upgrades.
Miguel (NetOps): Egress IPs: customers want a single advertised IP per region. Options:
- static egress via announced prefixes (we announce BGP)
- NAT gateway with predictable elastic IPs
- customer-managed egress (they control NAT)
We should document all three.
DevRel-J: Sales feedback: top asks are migration assistance, IP guarantees, and a clear rollback script. Many customers price runway around <2h maintenance windows.
Riya S.: Proposed GA scope (draft):
- Primary upgrade lane: blue-green swap for control-plane + runtime config changes (support for capacity doubling window)
- Secondary lane: rolling upgrades for minor non-breaking service patches
- Disallow DB migrations for GA rollouts; require offline migration plan for customers who need it
- GA networking: offer two transport modes: 1) peering with advertised IPs 2) transit VPN + NAT gateway
Nora (EngOps): Effort estimate: blue-green plumbing + IP swap automation ~5w, rolling automation + health probes ~3w, docs + runbooks ~1w. Testing matrix: include canary traffic split, failed deployment rollback, and simulated net partition.
Miguel (NetOps): We should include a network failure fallback: if peering loses route, automatically reroute to hosted endpoint in same region (token scoping required). Adds ~4d but reduces customer downtime.
DevRel-J: Pilot criteria suggestion:
- 2 pilot customers: one peering customer with static allowlist, one VPN + NAT customer
- Success metrics: <300ms median latency delta vs hosted, successful rollback within target SLO, no more than 1 manual intervention per pilot run
Nora (EngOps): Test plan snippet for pilots:
```
- create blue (v1) and green (v2) stacks in customer VPC
- validate health endpoints: /health, /kvcache/status
- attach advertised egress IP to green
- shift DNS / routing to green (5% -> 25% -> 100%)
- monitor token-scoped failover metrics
- if >2% errors during ramp -> automatic rollback to blue
```
Riya S.: Launch gates (draft):
- Gate 1: runbooks + customer comms templates (must)
- Gate 2: infra automation merged + e2e tests green
- Gate 3: two pilot customers completed and signed off
- Gate 4: security review + KMS + audit logs verified
- Gate 5: PS checklist and migration pricing published
Miguel (NetOps): Also require BGP announcement playbook if we support announced prefixes.
Nora (EngOps): Risk notes:
- DB migrations remain manual -> document clearly
- Airgapped installs need agent overlay (post-GA) and longer validation
- Double capacity window in blue-green may cost customers; include an opt-in toggle in runbook
Riya S.: Decision proposal (voting):
- GA upgrade lane = blue-green swap (primary) + rolling for small patches (secondary)
- GA networking = VPC peering with advertised/static egress OR transit VPN + NAT for customers who cannot peer
- Agent overlay = out-of-band GA (post-GA) for airgapped installs
React with :thumbsup: to approve or :warning: to raise blockers before Wed.
Tom H.: :thumbsup: from infra. We'll add cost guidance to runbook.
Miguel (NetOps): :thumbsup: but add BGP playbook and monitoring hook.
DevRel-J: :thumbsup: will coordinate pilots.
Nora (EngOps): :warning: request clarifying rollback SLO: can we commit to <1h for config-only?
Riya S.: We will commit to <1h rollback for config/control-plane-only changes, document DB migration exception. Adding to memo.
InfraBot: ticket created INF-4001: private-deploy-bluegreen-automation.
Riya S.: Next actions:
- @Nora (EngOps) break down INF-4001 into tasks and spike on BGP swap script by Mon EOD
- @Miguel (NetOps) draft BGP/NAT playbook and failure modes
- @DevRel-J identify two pilot customers and schedule pilot windows
I'll write a short decision memo after votes are tallied. Thanks all.
